answers.answer: 2 players: 4 Player cards each; 3 players: 3 each; 4 players: 2 each. Remove Epidemic cards before dealing; pawns start in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: remove Epidemic cards; starting hands table; matching colored pawns in Atlanta.

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2. Reveal 3 Infection cards and place 3 matching-color cubes in each named city; reveal 3 more and place 2 each; reveal 3 more and place 1 each. Put all 9 revealed cards on the Infection Discard Pile; remaining cards form the Infection Deck. The summary does not specify which deck end the remaining cards form from.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: leftmost “2”; three groups of three at 3, 2, and 1 cubes; all 9 to Infection Discard Pile; remaining cards form Infection Deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles as equal in size as possible, shuffle one Epidemic into each pile, then stack the piles with smaller piles on the bottom. Unused Epidemic cards are set aside before preparation; the summary does not further state their disposition.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 6–7: Epidemic cards are removed and set aside; difficulty counts; piles equal in number to Epidemics and as equal in size as possible; smaller piles on bottom.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions and actions may repeat. Whether a player may stop before taking all 4 is not explicitly stated. The destination for cards discarded to pay for actions is not stated. Then draw 2 Player cards, resolve any Epidemics, and discard down to 7; then infect cities by the current infection rate. After all three phases, play passes to the left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Do 4 Actions” (actions may repeat), “Draw 2 Player Cards,” “Infect Cities”; after all 3 phases, play passes to the left. Hand limit section says excess cards are discarded or played as Event cards.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry: move to a city connected by a white line, with no card cost stated. Direct Flight: discard the City card naming the destination. Charter Flight: discard the City card matching your current city to move to any city. Shuttle Flight: move between any two cities with research stations. White lines that go off one board edge wrap to the other edge (example: Sydney and Los Angeles). The destination of discarded movement cards is not specified.
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table; Special Rules: “Board wrapping: White lines going off one edge of the board wrap to the other edge.”

answers.answer: Normally, discard the City card matching your current city to place a station there. If all 6 are already built, move one from the board. The summary says that if more than 6 stations are supplied, set extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Build a Research Station action; Special Rules: research station limit and extras.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action by a non-Medic removes 1 cube of any color from the city; if that disease is cured, it removes all cubes of that color from the city instead. The summary does not say that a single action clears other colors, nor where removed cubes go.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: “Remove 1 disease cube of any color from your city. If that disease is cured, remove all cubes of that color from your city instead.”

answers.answer: At a research station, discard 5 City cards of the same color to cure that disease; the station city color need not match the disease. The summary says cubes may still be on the board at victory, but does not explicitly state what happens to existing cubes at the moment a cure is discovered. It does not say what happens if no cubes of that color are on the board.
answers.evidence: Discover a Cure action; Special Rules: any research station works; Victory: diseases need not be eradicated and cubes may still be on board.

answers.answer: Give or take the City card matching the city both players occupy; both players must agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they immediately discard or play an Event card. The summary does not specify whose agreement beyond saying both players agree.
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge action: matching current-city card, same city, both players must agree; recipient over 7 immediately discards or plays Event.

answers.answer: The Researcher may give any City card to a player in the same city. A player sharing with the Researcher on their turn may take any of the Researcher’s City cards. The summary does not state that the other player can give the Researcher an arbitrary nonmatching card using the Researcher exception; that part is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Roles: Researcher may give any City card; a player who Shares Knowledge with the Researcher on their turn may take any of the Researcher’s City cards.

answers.answer: After actions, if fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the game ends in a loss; do not reshuffle discards. The summary says to draw the top 2 Player cards but does not explicitly say whether they are drawn simultaneously or one at a time.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: “Draw the top 2 cards”; “If fewer than 2 cards remain when you need to draw, the game ends”; “do not reshuffle discards.”

answers.answer: Resolve Epidemic steps in order: Increase the Infection Rate marker by 1; Infect by drawing the bottom Infection card. Since the named city has two cubes of that color, add only enough to reach 3 (one cube), then an outbreak occurs. Discard that Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile. Intensify by reshuffling only the Infection Discard Pile and placing it on top of the Infection Deck. Resolved Epidemic cards are removed from the game; do not draw replacements.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: Increase, Infect (add only enough to reach 3, then outbreak), discard Infection card, Intensify; “Do not draw replacements.”

answers.answer: After 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics respectively, flip 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4 Infection cards per turn.
answers.evidence: Infection Rate Track table: Epidemics Resolved 0–6 maps to Cards Flipped 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.

answers.answer: Resolve the first Epidemic completely, then the second completely; Events may be played between them. The summary says to discard down to 7 after resolving any Epidemics drawn, but does not specify when hand reduction occurs relative to the two Epidemics if the hand is over limit.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: for two drawn at once, resolve all steps for first then all steps for second; Events may be played between. Turn Structure: resolve any Epidemics drawn, then discard down to 7-card hand limit.

answers.answer: Flip Infection cards from the top of the Infection Deck equal to the current infection rate, one at a time. For each, place one matching-color cube in the named city unless the disease is eradicated; if that city already has 3 of that color, place no fourth cube and cause an outbreak. A disease that is cured but not eradicated is not exempted from placement in the summary’s infection rule, so it receives the normal placement/outbreak resolution. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: top of Infection Deck; one cube unless eradicated; at 3 cubes no fourth, outbreak; discard each card to Infection Discard Pile.

answers.answer: The first outbreak advances the marker once and places one cube in each connected city. A connected city already at 3 cubes triggers a chain reaction after the current outbreak resolves, advancing the marker for that outbreak. During chain reactions, do not add cubes to cities that already had an outbreak while resolving this Infection card, so the first city does not receive a return cube if it already outbreaked. Different colors have separate limits: a city may have up to 3 cubes of each color.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: marker advances; spread to every connected city; chain reaction after current outbreak resolves; no cubes added to cities that already had an outbreak; up to 3 of each color.

answers.answer: No. Airlift cannot be played between drawing an Infection card and resolving it, so it cannot move the Quarantine Specialist before that card’s outbreak resolves. An Event can be played at any time except between drawing and resolving a card; therefore it may be played after resolving the current card and before the next card. The player who plays it chooses its use. It costs no action, and played Event cards go to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: any time (not an action), cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card, player decides use, discard to Player Discard Pile. Airlift moves any 1 pawn.

answers.answer: As an action, the Contingency Planner takes 1 Event card from the Player Discard Pile and stores it on the Role card. Capacity is 1 and it does not count against the hand limit. The summary gives no restriction by discard-pile depth. When played, remove that Event from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Contingency Planner role: action; take 1 Event from Player Discard Pile; limit 1; not hand-limit counted; when played, remove from game.

answers.answer: As an action, Dispatcher may move any pawn (with its owner’s permission) to a city with another pawn, or move another player’s pawn as if it were their own. Direct and Charter Flight discards come from the Dispatcher’s hand. Charter Flight requires the City card matching the city the moving pawn is in. The summary does not state whether Dispatcher may direct another pawn to Treat Disease. Dispatcher cannot use the Operations Expert’s special move.
answers.evidence: Dispatcher role: both movement options and permission; discards from Dispatcher’s hand for Direct/Charter Flights; cannot use Operations Expert’s special move. Charter Flight action: discard card matching current city.

answers.answer: Players win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; diseases need not be eradicated and cubes may remain on the board. The three loss triggers are: the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (8th outbreak); the needed disease cubes cannot be placed, during an epidemic, outbreak, or infection (immediate loss); or a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after their actions (Player Deck exhaustion).
answers.evidence: Victory and Defeat sections; Special Rules: cube supply check causes immediate loss.
